author.name: Mara Ellison
author.bio_short: Mara Ellison writes about the quiet mathematics of leaving, returning, and finding a place to stand.
author.bio: Mara Ellison is a novelist drawn to tidal towns, unfinished maps, and the small decisions that change a life's direction. Her work follows people who make their way through complicated inheritances with patience, wit, and a stubborn tenderness for the places that made them. She lives near the water and keeps a notebook for sentences overheard on long walks.

headline: Stories for the way back
intro: Mara Ellison writes luminous, searching fiction about departure, memory, and the landscapes we carry home.

books.title: The Shape of Returning
books.subtitle: A novel
books.description: After a decade away, cartographer Lena Vale comes back to the river town she once promised never to see again. As the old ferry route disappears beneath a changing shoreline, she must redraw the map of a family story that was never hers alone to tell.
books.hook: A cartographer returns to a river town and discovers that home has been changing in her absence.

books.title: Where the River Ends
books.subtitle: Stories
books.description: In these linked stories, women and men stand at the edges of familiar lives: a mother measures a vanished coastline, a brother keeps watch at a closed station, and a child learns the names of every bridge between here and elsewhere.
books.hook: Linked stories about the thresholds where a life can open, close, or change course.

contact.headline: Write to Mara
contact.message: For reading group conversations, event invitations, or a note about the books, send a message here. Mara reads every letter when she can.

excerpt: At the bend in the river, Lena stopped walking. The water had taken the old road with it, but the willows still leaned toward the missing bridge, keeping faith with a crossing no one could see.
